001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jfr;
002
003import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
004
005import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogAlerts;
006import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
007import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter;
008import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable;
009
010/**
011 * A {@link LogAlerts.Listener} that commits each alert as its own
012 * {@link RainbowGumAlertEvent} - deliberately a separate JFR event type family from
013 * {@link JfrLogOutput}'s {@link RainbowGumLogEvent}, even though the shape (per-level
014 * split, same fields) and rendering are the same; see {@link RainbowGumAlertEvent} for
015 * why sharing one event type between alerts and application log lines was rejected.
016 * <p>
017 * Alerts are rare and already delivered synchronously one at a time (see
018 * {@link LogAlerts#addListener(LogAlerts.Listener)}), so unlike {@link JfrLogOutput} this
019 * renders the message directly with {@link JfrLogOutput#MESSAGE_FORMATTER} instead of
020 * going through the buffered {@code LogEncoder}/{@code LogOutput} machinery meant for a
021 * high volume appender.
022 *
023 * @see JfrAlertListenerBuilder
024 * @see JfrAlertListenerConfigurator
025 */
026public final class JfrAlertListener implements LogAlerts.Listener {
027
028        private final boolean enabled;
029
030        /**
031         * Creates a JFR alert listener. Not gated on {@code enabled} itself - see
032         * {@link JfrAlertListener#enabled()} and {@link JfrAlertListenerConfigurator}, which
033         * builds this unconditionally and only then decides whether to register it.
034         * @param enabled whether this listener should actually be registered; see
035         * {@link JfrAlertListener#enabled()}. Default {@code false}.
036         * @return listener.
037         */
038        @LogConfigurable(name = "JfrAlertListenerBuilder", prefix = "logging.jfr.alerts.")
039        static JfrAlertListener of(@Nullable Boolean enabled) {
040                return new JfrAlertListener(enabled != null && enabled);
041        }
042
043        private JfrAlertListener(boolean enabled) {
044                this.enabled = enabled;
045        }
046
047        /**
048         * Whether this listener should actually be registered with
049         * {@link LogAlerts#addListener(LogAlerts.Listener)}.
050         * @return enabled.
051         */
052        public boolean enabled() {
053                return enabled;
054        }
055
056        @Override
057        public void onAlert(LogEvent event) {
058                var jfrEvent = RainbowGumAlertEvent.of(event.level());
059                if (jfrEvent == null || !jfrEvent.isEnabled()) {
060                        return;
061                }
062                var message = new StringBuilder();
063                JfrLogOutput.MESSAGE_FORMATTER.format(message, event);
064                jfrEvent.message = message.toString();
065                jfrEvent.logger = event.loggerName();
066                var t = event.throwableOrNull();
067                if (t != null) {
068                        var stackTrace = new StringBuilder();
069                        ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(stackTrace, t);
070                        jfrEvent.throwable = stackTrace.toString();
071                }
072                jfrEvent.commit();
073        }
074
075}
